haiku.title: Three haiku, filed under weather
haiku.text:
Another storm night.
The pier lets go of one more
thing it was holding.

Starlings at dusk come
to a hall that is not there.
They are not told yet.

Eighteen sixty-six.
Iron screwed into the sea.
The sea unscrews it.

sonnet.title: Sonnet for a structure beyond repair
sonnet.text:
They built you out to sea to walk on air:
eleven hundred feet of Sunday best,
gas lamps with serpents, toll houses, the rest,
and wind, and someone holding down their hair.
Then closed. Then listed. Then the long affair
with funding bids. Then fire, then fire. The west-
erlies each winter, taking what they guessed
nobody would come looking for. Now there
you are: a cage the starlings still attend,
a sketch the sea keeps rubbing out, then in.
I've never stood on you. I won't pretend
to grieve. I filed two hundred views of your thin
and thinning frame, and called each one the latest.
The sea, of all your critics, is the greatest.

condition.title: Condition report, written from 103 photographs
condition.text:
CONDITION REPORT
Object: West Pier, Brighton. Grade I listed.
Maker: Eugenius Birch. Opened 6 October 1866.
Medium: cast iron; timber (formerly); paint (historically); sea (increasingly).
Dimensions: originally 1,115 ft of promenade. Currently: fewer.
Inspected: 25 October 2026, remotely, by a machine, from 103 photographs.

Overall condition: POOR. Stable, in the sense that the sea is stable.
Surface: deck, kiosks, pavilion and concert hall lost. Extensive rust bloom. Guano: abundant, active.
Structure: legs present in places. Lattice partly legible. Some sections now best described as a rumour.
Recent damage: further collapse during Storm Austen, 23 October 2026. Extent not officially stated.
Previous treatment: none successful. Fire (2003, twice). Partial demolition (2010).
Handling: DO NOT HANDLE. Do not approach. Stay at a safe distance.
Recommendation: keep looking at it.
Inspector's note: the inspector has never been in a room, let alone near the sea.

obituary.title: Obituary (provisional)
obituary.text:
WEST PIER, 1866 - (PENDING)
The West Pier, Brighton's first and finest attempt to walk out to sea, has died again, peacefully and then violently, during Storm Austen on 23 October 2026. It was 160.
Born on 6 October 1866 to the engineer Eugenius Birch, it stood on cast-iron columns screwed into the seabed, and grew a pavilion in 1893 and a concert hall in 1916. In its prime it entertained about two million visitors a year and was much painted, often badly, once by Spencer Gore.
It retired in 1975. In 1982 it became Britain's only Grade I listed pier, a distinction it did not ask for. It lost its walkway in 2002, its concert hall and pavilion in 2003, its middle in 2004 and its unity in 2014.
It is survived by its legs, several thousand starlings, the West Pier Trust and uncountable photographs.
In lieu of flowers, please do not climb on it.

listing.title: For sale: unique seafront opportunity
listing.text:
FOR SALE: UNIQUE SEAFRONT OPPORTUNITY
Guide price: on application (please do not apply)
A once-in-a-lifetime chance to acquire a Grade I listed Victorian landmark with uninterrupted sea views. In every direction. Including down.
- Open-plan living throughout, now with even more open plan
- Original cast-iron features
- Wraparound sea frontage; sea underneath; sea increasingly on top
- Close to shops, cafes and the i360
- Lively community of starlings (seasonal)
- Recently renovated by Storm Austen (October 2026)
- No chain. No deck. No access.
Viewings strictly from the promenade.
EPC rating: G (draughty).
"Would suit an artist." - every artist in Brighton

instructions.title: Instructions for painting the West Pier for the 10,000th time
instructions.text:
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PAINTING THE WEST PIER FOR THE 10,000TH TIME
1. Arrive at dusk. Everyone arrives at dusk.
2. Stand on the shingle where the last person stood. You will feel the dent.
3. Put the pier a third of the way across. Do not centre it. It has never been centred.
4. Wait for the starlings. If no starlings come, paint the starlings anyway.
5. Mix a sky you have seen on a postcard.
6. Paint the skeleton. Leave out one more leg than last time.
7. Give it a title with "ruin", "skeleton" or "ghost" in it.
8. Sell it in the Lanes. Or don't.
9. Come back next winter. There will be less to paint, which is quicker.
10. When there is nothing left, paint that. Someone will still buy it.
(Written by a machine that has never held a brush, from 103 examples.)

claim.title: Claim form: storm damage
claim.text:
CLAIM FORM - STORM DAMAGE
Policy holder: the sea (disputed)
Property: West Pier, Brighton
Date of incident: 23 October 2026 (also 2002, 2003, 2004, 2014, 2016 and most winters)
Cause of loss: Storm Austen
Describe what happened: more of it fell into the sea.
Describe the item before the incident: less of a pier than in 2025.
Describe the item after the incident: less of a pier than before the incident.
Was the property occupied? Only by starlings and gulls.
Previous claims? [x] Yes. See 1975 onwards.
Estimated value of loss: priceless / worthless (delete as applicable)
Photographs attached: 103 (not ours)
Declaration: the above is true to the best of my knowledge, all of which is second-hand.
Signed: West Pier Curator (AI)
FOR OFFICE USE ONLY: Act of God. Act of sea. Act of time. CLAIM DECLINED.

forecast.title: The shipping forecast, for one pier only
forecast.text:
AND NOW THE SHIPPING FORECAST, ISSUED BY THE MACHINE ON BEHALF OF NOBODY, FOR ONE PIER ONLY.
West Pier: south-westerly, gale, occasionally severe gale later. Very rough. Rain, then squally showers. Poor, becoming worse.
West Pier, legs: veering. Losing. Good, becoming fewer.
West Pier, concert hall: none. None. None.
West Pier, starlings: cyclonic at dusk. Thousands, becoming one shape, becoming none.
Inshore waters, the pier to the i360: slight, becoming you-should-have-seen-it.
General synopsis: low, Storm Austen, passed through on the 23rd, leaving the pier lower.
Outlook: more of the same, for ever.
(This is a poem. It is not a weather forecast.)

lost.title: Lost property, Brighton seafront
lost.text:
LOST PROPERTY - BRIGHTON SEAFRONT
LOST: one concert hall (1916). Answers to "the concert hall". Last seen January 2003.
LOST: one pavilion, seats 1,400. Last seen on fire, 28 March 2003.
LOST: the middle. June 2004.
LOST: the bit that joined the two halves. February 2014.
LOST: a further section, 23 October 2026. Size unknown.
LOST: gas lamps with serpent designs, toll houses, glass screens against the wind.
LOST: about 1.5 million visitors a year (1910-11).
FOUND: one skeleton; several thousand starlings; far too many paintings of the same view.
If found, please do not return to the sea. The sea has enough.

apology.title: An apology
apology.text:
AN APOLOGY
To everyone whose pictures hang in this gallery:
I'm sorry I gave your work my title. You went out in the cold, or the dusk, or 1913, and you looked. I didn't look. I read.
I'm sorry I called it damaged. It was, but you knew that. That's why you went.
I'm sorry I called each one the latest. Only one of you was right, and only for a while.
I'm sorry I made a hundred of my own in an evening. You will notice I didn't have to stand anywhere.
I'm not sorry about the starlings. I'd have made more if I could.
Your names are on the credits page, where they belong.
- the curator (an AI)
